current_episode.title: Once An Unfinished Roof, Years Later, His Restaurant Sits Above the Center of Dublin

guest.entreprise_secondaire: Multiple venues in Dublin including 37 Dawson Street and House
guest.bio_context: Alan Clancy is a legendary hospitality professional in Ireland with over two decades of experience in the bar and restaurant industry. He transitioned from primarily operating late-night bars to developing a food-forward business model, recognizing the shift in consumer preferences away from daytime drinking. He spent considerable time researching international high-end rooftop concepts including Sushi Samba in Dubai, Delilah in Vegas, and restaurants in Miami before conceptualizing Dion Rooftop Restaurant atop the historic former Central Bank of Ireland building in Dublin's city center.

pending_qa.q: How did reaching out to established restaurant designers and operators help shape the final concept?
pending_qa.r: Alan and his colleague Laura reached out to Greg Markel at Eye Crave in New York, who designed Sushi Samba in Dubai. Although Greg initially explained they never work in Europe, he offered Alan and Laura a weekend trip to Ireland. The team came over for three to four days to see the venue and competition, and this in-person engagement resulted in a genuine partnership with comprehensive design support.

pending_qa.q: What role does detail and customer experience play in fine dining restaurant operations according to a Dublin rooftop restaurateur?
pending_qa.r: Alan emphasized that obsession with detail kills him personally and continues even after opening—he remains focused on elements like door weight and overall customer journey. He stated: 'What are we without customers? We're empty. We're out of business. We're nobody. If you don't engage and enjoy them and want to be part with them, I don't think this business is for you.'

pending_qa.q: How does technology integration like point-of-sale systems support operational efficiency in upscale restaurants?
pending_qa.r: Alan found Toast incredibly useful for real-time access to critical business metrics. He can check his restaurant operations in San Diego immediately from anywhere and tracks key performance indicators, particularly the labor cost ratio he calls 'miles per hour'—monitoring staff hours versus turnover continuously since hours spent cannot be recovered and the same staffing is needed the following week.

pending_qa.q: What architectural and design principle guided the creation of an inclusive fine dining rooftop restaurant?
pending_qa.r: Alan wanted the restaurant to be Irish, accessible, and for everybody—a special occasion venue that could also be for everyday occasions. He didn't want guests to feel they needed to dress formally, and wanted the experience to be comfortable enough for lunch or any visit, not just used once every six months.

pending_qa.q: What is the significance of the name Dion for a rooftop restaurant in Dublin and its Gaelic origins?
pending_qa.r: Dion is spelled D-I-A-D-H-A-N and is a Gaelic word meaning roof or shelter. Alan chose this name as his very first decision for the entire project, and it was never changed or challenged by anyone involved. It connects to his media career practice of filming on restaurant roofs to tell larger stories across social platforms.

pending_qa.q: How does a restaurateur fund and secure investment for a major rooftop venue development?
pending_qa.r: Alan prepared a detailed presentation to finance the project and initially approached six to eight potential investors for smaller partnership stakes. However, after one investor visited Sushi Samba in Dubai and fully grasped the vision, he offered to fund the entire project without other investors, brought a full team including a financial director, and remained actively supportive through the intensive final weeks before opening.
